chunks: And Muhammad ibn Ja'far narrated to me, saying: He narrated to me from Muhammad ibn al-Husayn, from Ja'far ibn Bashir, from Hammad ibn Isa, from Rib'i ibn Abdullah, from al-Fudayl ibn Yasar, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: O Fudayl! How negligent you people are! You do not go to the Ziyarah of al-Husayn (peace be upon him). Do you not know that there are four thousand angels, disheveled and covered with dust, who weep for him until the Day of Judgment?

key_terms.أَجْفَاكُمْ: How negligent you are / How distant you have become
key_terms.تَزُورُونَ: You visit (specifically referring to Ziyarah of the Imams)
key_terms.شُعْثاً غُبْراً: Disheveled and covered with dust (a sign of deep mourning)

ai.seo_question: What is the significance of angels weeping for Imam Husayn in Shia tradition?
ai.summary: In *Kamil al-Ziyarah*, Ibn Qulawayh records Imam al-Sadiq’s poignant rebuke to Fudayl ibn Yasar for neglecting the visitation of Imam al-Husayn, linking human devotion to cosmic reality. The image of four thousand angels, described as 'shuuthan ghubran' (disheveled and dusty), signifies their humble, continuous mourning, illustrating that the Imam’s presence bridges the earthly and celestial realms. This hadith underscores the Shia theological view that Ziyarah is not merely a ritual but a participation in the eternal grief of the heavens.

en.sayyid-mohsen-al-husayni-al-milani: 6. Muḥammad ibn Ja’far narrated to me from Muḥammad ibn Ḥusain, from Ja’far ibn Bashīr, from Ḥammād ibn ‘Isā, from Rib’i ibn ‘Abdillāh, from Fuďayl ibn Yasār, who said:

Abū ‘Abdillāh (Imam Sādiq (a.s.)) said: O Fuďayl! How negligent you people are!!! You do not go to the Ziyārah of Ḥusain (a.s.)!!! Do you not know that there are four thousand angels who are disheveled and covered with dust who continuously cry over Ḥusain (a.s.) (and will continue to do so) until the Day of Judgment?
